answer: Give each agent identity a sequential puzzle that only moves forward one step at a time, like climbing toward a summit where no shortcut exists. A single operator cannot speed many copies up in parallel, because each step depends on the last and cannot be shared or outsourced. A new agent starts in the sable shadow of unproven status and earns trust only as its puzzle chain advances in public. If a whisper of identical step sequences ever appears from two identities, the network treats them as one operator and merges their rewards, so cloning adds cost without adding income.
